purpose: Rigorous external references and formal-library provenance for student-facing Samplinglib theorem pages. These entries distinguish Chewi's source statement from ASTIS-added proof detail and from external formal-library reuse.

entries.heading: Rigorous references: stopping times and localization
astis_additions: ASTIS exposes the filtration-measurability obligation for every hitting/localizing time instead of treating it as an implicit textbook step.

For the canonical energy localizer, ASTIS separates pathwise continuity of accumulated energy, closedness of the equality-level set, attainment of the infimum, the no-overshoot bound, and the measurable stopping-time criterion.
The localizing-sequence claim is not closed by metadata: its finite stopped L2 energy and almost-sure exhaustion are separate compiled obligations.

references.label: Karatzas–Shreve, Brownian Motion and Stochastic Calculus, 2nd ed.
references.note: Chapter 1 develops martingales, stopping times, and filtrations; Chapter 3 develops stochastic integration. Use this as a rigorous probability-theory reference parallel to Chewi's primer.

references.label: Revuz–Yor, Continuous Martingales and Brownian Motion, 3rd ed.
references.note: A standard detailed reference for continuous martingales, stochastic integration, localization, and Brownian-motion techniques.

references.label: Mathlib: Stopping times, stopped processes and stopped values
references.note: Provides MeasureTheory.IsStoppingTime and stopped-process infrastructure. ASTIS reuses these interfaces where their hypotheses match the textbook route.

entries.heading: Rigorous references: Itô integration, stopping, and local martingales
astis_additions: ASTIS builds the Itô integral from elementary adapted processes through the L2 isometry/completion route, rather than postulating an ItoIntegral contract.

The localization route records the endpoint convention explicitly: for a stopping time inside a grid cell, one must preserve the final partial Brownian increment rather than simply drop the whole cell coefficient.
The target identity is therefore proved first for grid-valued stops, then transported to general stopping times through approximation and L2/continuous-path limits before local-martingale gluing.

references.label: Kiyosi Itô (1944), Stochastic Integral
references.note: The original 1944 paper, Proceedings of the Imperial Academy, volume 20, issue 8, pages 519–524, DOI 10.3792/pia/1195572786.

references.label: Karatzas–Shreve, Brownian Motion and Stochastic Calculus, 2nd ed.
references.note: Chapter 3 is a systematic treatment of stochastic integration and is the main external textbook cross-check for the L2 construction and stopping arguments.

references.label: Revuz–Yor, Continuous Martingales and Brownian Motion, 3rd ed.
references.note: Contains an extensive stochastic-integration chapter and the continuous-local-martingale viewpoint used by the localization route.

references.label: Mathlib: Optional stopping theorem
references.note: Formal optional-stopping infrastructure for stopped martingales. ASTIS cites it as external formal-library provenance, but does not use it to skip the separate stochastic-integral stopping identity required here.

references.label: Mathlib: Optional sampling theorem
references.note: Formal conditional-expectation identities at bounded stopping times; useful downstream once the relevant stopped Itô process has actually been constructed.

references.label: Ying–Degenne, A Formalization of Doob's Martingale Convergence Theorems in mathlib
references.note: Documents foundational mathlib work on conditional expectation, stochastic processes, stopping times, martingales, and Doob-style convergence theory.
